sentences.text: Here’s the heart of Rule nineteen, and it’s for the boat with radar.
If you detect another vessel by radar alone, you must work out whether a close-quarters situation is developing, or a risk of collision exists.
If it is, you take avoiding action in ample time.
And if that action is a change of course, there are two things to avoid, so far as possible.
First: avoid altering course to port for a vessel forward of your beam, unless you’re overtaking her.
Second: avoid altering course toward a vessel that’s abeam or abaft your beam.
Put those together and the pattern is simple.
For a target ahead of you, don’t turn left.
For a target beside or behind you, don’t turn toward her.
So for a vessel ahead, a substantial turn to starboard is usually the safe choice.
And slowing down, or stopping, is always allowed.
